Token usage from harness usage.total_tokens — input + output + cache_creation; cache_read excluded. audit, readme-drift-sync, skill-usage stay null here because they're in SKILL-CALIBRATION-HAIKU-SAMPLE-LATEST.json (overlay reads both); ai-codegen-smell-audit arm A hit session-token wall in batch 2 (arm B captured only). session-cost arm A produced an incomplete answer (only main thread, no sub-agents — same baseline-behavior pattern as the Opus session-cost where arm A counted cache_read). skills.notes: CORRECTNESS-not-tokens win for the recipe. Haiku arm A measured only main thread (10.6M tokens reported, missed sub-agents); arm B followed the SKILL.md and walked sub-agent JSONLs too (20.6M tokens reported, correct). Arm B paid more TOKENS to do more thorough work — the -89% pct_saved here understates the recipe's value: it's a correctness win, not a compression win. Same pattern as the Opus session-cost (arm A counted cache_read incorrectly).

skills.name: skill-calibration

caveats: Aggregate covers 7 of 8 library skills (audit/readme-drift-sync/skill-usage in SAMPLE; ai-codegen-smell-audit arm A pending re-dispatch).

Haiku -15% vs Sonnet -13% — essentially identical on the complete-able subset. The batch-1 caveat about Haiku narrowing the cost-more from -27% to -17% was a partial-data artifact; with 3 more skills in (session-cost especially), the aggregate matches Sonnet closely.

Bimodal composition still visible: mikko-install NARROWS (Sonnet -35% → Haiku -14%, +21pp), mikko-help WIDENS (Sonnet -22% → Haiku -62%, -40pp), and session-cost has a methodology-shaped cost (arm B paid 2x to walk sub-agents correctly). Aggregate hides these.
